fix: In 'X above, Y beneath', 'above' means the upper (adaxial) side and 'beneath' the lower (abaxial) side. Put the colour on that side, not on the whole blade.
reason: The flora says the leaves are dark green above and paler beneath, so 'whole blade dark green' is false without the adaxial side.
'Ovules 5 or 6' is a count of ovules with values 5 and 6.

fix: 'glaucous' means covered with a waxy bloom. It is not a green colour.
reason: The stem is glaucous, and nothing in the flora says it is green.
The ultimate (leaflet) blades are approximately lanceolate. A leaf-lamina bearer with an 'approximately' qualifier fits.
'Subequal' petals means petals of nearly equal size, which matches equal + approximately, as in the earlier review of 'subequal'.
The adaxial leaf surface is glabrous, and the adaxial-epidermis bearer is right.

fix: In 'without deep reticulate veins', the negation applies to the vein pattern (deep, reticulate), not to the veins being there. Read it as 'veins not deeply reticulate/impressed abaxially', or leave it unannotated. Never read it as 'vascular bundle absent'.
reason: The blade has veins. The flora only denies that they are deeply reticulate on the lower side.
Cauline leaves 3–7 cm long, with the cauline context kept.
The leaflet's lower side has denser simple and bifid hairs. Lower-surface bearer with a hairy quality is right.

fix: In 'yellowish appressed-puberulous', the colour word describes the hairs (indumentum), not the organ. The organ's own colour comes later: 'yellow to orange at maturity'.
reason: 'Yellowish' qualifies the puberulous hairs. The receptacle is called yellow to orange only at maturity, which is a separate statement.
Fruit orange at maturity, with the mature context kept.
7–9 lateral veins on each side of the midrib, with the position kept.
Leaves numerous: present, with amount 'many'.
Calyx segments sparingly puberulent: sepal with pubescent hairs.
Seeds numerous: present, with amount 'many'.
Petals 18–35 mm long.

fix: In 'attached to base of X', the target is the base of X. Keep the whole (corolla tube) and not only a generic 'plant organ base'.
reason: The stamens are attached to the base of the corolla tube. 'Attached to a base' alone loses which organ it is.

fix: An 'apex ...' that follows a sub-part already named in the same clause ('distal leaf sheaths ..., apex acute') belongs to that sub-part, not to the header part 'Leaves:'.
reason: The acute or subacute apex belongs to the distal leaf sheaths (Eleocharis leaves are reduced to sheaths), not to a leaf blade.

fix: A part followed by a shape word ('Capsule obovoid') should give the shape, not only 'present'.
reason: The flora gives the capsule's shape, obovoid. 'Present' loses what was said.
Cauline leaves ovate-triangular. Basal leaves are absent, so all the leaves are cauline, and the leaf bearer with the ovate-to-triangular continuum is fine.
Fibrous roots numerous: roots present, with amount 'many'.

fix: An adverb of side placed before the quality ('adaxially glabrescent', 'abaxially villous') should move the bearer to that surface, as is already done for 'adaxial ...' in A01565.
reason: Only the upper side of the outer leaves is glabrescent. The lower side is villous, so 'leaf glabrescent' is false as stated.
The umbel is densely many-flowered: flowers present, many, inside the inflorescence.
In FNA, 'herbs h × w' gives height × width, so the width is 5–10 dm (50–100 cm), converted correctly.
The corolla lobes (petal parts) are much longer than the stamens, which matches increased length relative to the stamens.

fix: 'the mid-leaflet N long, M wide' measures one leaflet. Keep the position (terminal/middle leaflet).
reason: Only the middle leaflet is 3–4 cm wide. The lateral leaflets are smaller, so the width does not hold for all leaflets.
'Stems and petioles ... not viscid' applies to the petioles too.

fix: In Selaginella, 'Dorsal leaves ...' and 'Ventral leaves ...' are separate kinds of leaf. Keep the position slot.
reason: 'Not carinate' is said of the dorsal leaves only. The ventral leaves are described separately.

fix: 'Repand' (wavy-edged) describes a margin. When it follows a list of margin spines, the bearer is the leaf margin, not the whole leaf.
reason: 'More or less repand' follows the margin spines and describes the leaf edge.

fix: 'to N mm' gives only an upper bound. Do not store it as the range N–N. Here the lower bound is the 2.5 mm at anthesis.
reason: The calyx lobes grow up to 4 mm in fruit. They are not exactly 4 mm.
